vocabulary.definition: the emission of energy as electromagnetic waves or as moving subatomic particles, especially high-energy particles that cause ionization
vocabulary.example: The doctor explained the risks of exposure to radiation during the X-ray procedure.

vocabulary.definition: the splitting of an atomic nucleus into two or more lighter nuclei, accompanied by the release of energy
vocabulary.example: Nuclear power plants use nuclear fission to generate electricity.

vocabulary.definition: to increase the proportion of a particular isotope in an element, especially the proportion of U-235 in uranium
vocabulary.example: The enriched uranium was carefully monitored to ensure its safe handling.

vocabulary.definition: a collection of weapons and military equipment
vocabulary.example: The country invested heavily in building up its nuclear arsenal.

vocabulary.definition: the rapid increase in the number or amount of something
vocabulary.example: There are concerns about the proliferation of nuclear weapons worldwide.

vocabulary.definition: relating to or using nuclear reactions that occur only at very high temperatures
vocabulary.example: The thermonuclear bomb produced a devastating explosion.
